guideposts.label: The longest stage of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: With 210.8 kilometres from Vélez-Málaga to Peñas Blancas, today is the longest stage of La Vuelta 26. The other 200+ kilometres stage of this edition was on day 2 (Monaco > Manosque, 202.1 km). But it was a rolling day, while today is a proper mountain stage, with over 4,000 metres of elevation gain. Will it also make for the longest day on the saddle? So far, the record was set at Alto de Aitana,

guideposts.label: Welcome to Malaga
guideposts.detail: After Almeria, Granada, Jaen, Cordoba, Huelva, Seville, and Cadiz, La Vuelta 26 completes its Andalusian tour with a stage entirely set in the province of Malaga, the autonomous community’s eighth province. The race will then return to Granada for the final two stages of La Vuelta 26. Vélez-Málaga is a stage town for the second time in La Vuelta history, having hosted the start of stage 4 in 2018.

guideposts.label: Luis Angel Maté, the local icon
guideposts.detail: When stage 4 of La Vuelta 2018 set off from Vélez-Málaga, Luis Angel Maté also made the breakaway, defending his polka dot jersey and finishing 4th of the stage. Known as “El lince de Marbella” (Marbella’s lynx), he is an iconic cycling figure from the province of Malaga with 12 La Vuelta participations until he retired after the 2024 edition. guideposts.label: 10 years ago…
guideposts.detail: On 11 September 2016, Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) won in Madrid the final stage of La Vuelta 16, three days after opening his Grand Tour tally in Gandia (stage 18). At the time, he was 23 and claimed his first successes away from Scandinavia. guideposts.label: La Roja
guideposts.detail: Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) was the best of the GC contenders in the ITT, but Enric Mas (Movistar) surpassed the expectations as he only lost 33 seconds to the Slovenian. Roglic is back in second place, 1’37’’ behind the Spaniard. Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) fell down to third place, with a gap 3’01’’. The trio are set to battle for the podium while Richard Carapaz (EF Education-Eas

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: With Callum Thornley, Primoz Roglic and Finn Ficher-Black, Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe had the strongest collective performance yesterday. Decathlon CMA CGM still lead the overall team standings with a gap of 56’34’’ to XDS Astana and 1h13’46’’ to EF Education-EasyPost.

guideposts.label: Roads that witnessed La Vuelta history
guideposts.detail: The area has often been visited by La Vuelta, as illustrated by some of the stages passed on today’s route: - Rincon de la Victoria (km 13) saw Michael Storer win 10 in 2021, with Mauri Vansevenant in second place - Coin (km 61) hosted the start of stage 13 in 2017: MatteoTrentin won in Tomares with Gianni Moscon in second place - Yunquera (km 88.2) saw Ben O’Connor win stage 6 of La Vuelta 24 and

guideposts.label: First attacks
guideposts.detail: A group of six riders opened a small gap but the bunch is packed at km 2.

guideposts.label: Attacks keep flying
guideposts.detail: A lone rider opened a gap, five more attackers joined him, and no they're eight leaders at km 5!

guideposts.label: Grouped peloton
No risks, no glory?
guideposts.detail: The bunch is packed at km 10, just before Rincon de la Victoria, where Michael Storer won stage of La Vuelta 21. That day, Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora_hansgrohe) attacked, crashed, and famously said: “No risk, no glory”. Are the Slovenian star and his team ready to risk it all in the final stages of La Vuetla 26? “Today and tomorrow are two days where that quote is perfect to use", Callum Thornle

guideposts.label: 2 riders on the move: Wilksch and Wenzel
guideposts.detail: Hannes Wilksch (Tudor) and Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) are 12 seconds ahead of the peloton at km 13. Rudy Porter (Jayco AlUla) is in between.

guideposts.label: 4 chasers
guideposts.detail: Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), Lennard Kämna (Lidl-Trek) and Timo De Jong (Picnic PostNL) are with Rudy Porter (Jayco AlUla).

guideposts.label: The attackers are caught at km 19
guideposts.detail: The route is absolutely flat until Malaga (km 27.4). Then, there will be some gentle hills before the proper ascents of the day.

guideposts.label: 8 riders on the move
guideposts.detail: They've set off at km 21.

guideposts.label: Back together at km 22
guideposts.detail: Breakaway artist and La Vuelta veteran Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH) spoke about the race dynamics he expected for today's stage: "I reckon a very large breakaway of around 20–30 riders could form, just like on other days, with riders who aren’t too close in the general classification, and that breakaway could gain some time. And then, once we’re in there, we’ll see who the strongest ones ar

guideposts.label: Paul Double withdraws from La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: The British puncheur confessed last week he was struggling a lot and felt like "one of the worst riders inthe race at the moment". He tried to hang and was penultimate in the overall standings.

guideposts.label: More attacks...
guideposts.detail: But the bunch is packed at km 29.

guideposts.label: 3 attackers: Kruijswijk, Leknessund, Sütterlin
guideposts.detail: Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike), Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) and Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) are 15 seconds ahead of the peloton at km 34.

guideposts.label: The leading trio
The battle goes on
guideposts.detail: The three leaders are now riding 22 seconds ahead of the bunch, and there's one chaser in between.

guideposts.label: Coquard in pursuit?
guideposts.detail: Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) attacked from the bunch but he's rapidly been reeled in.

guideposts.label: More riders want to make the break
guideposts.detail: But the bunch cover all the counter-attacks at the moment. Meanxhile, the leading trio push their advantage to 42''.

guideposts.label: Steven Krujswijk, Andreas Leknessund and Jasha Sütterlin
Leknessund, Kruijswijk and Sütterlin have already covered 50 km
guideposts.detail: +32'' Three chasers +40'' Peloton

guideposts.label: Oliveira joins the first chase group
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, Kämna, Marti and Wenzel are caught by the bunch.

guideposts.label: 6 leaders after almost 60 kilometres
guideposts.detail: Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), Bastien Tronchon (Groupama-FDJ United) and Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility) join Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike), Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) and Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla). The peloton trail by 27''. Fabian Weiss (Tudor) has been caught.

guideposts.label: 7 leaders, including two UAE Emirates XRG riders
guideposts.detail: Ivo Oliveira dropped back momentarily to help Kevin Vermaerke close the gap.

guideposts.label: Sütterlin struggles to keep up at the front
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, Iñigo Elosegui (Kern Pharma) and riders from XDS Astana increase the pace in the peloton. The gap is down to 15'' with 130 kilometres to go.

guideposts.label: Dunbar sets off from the bunch
guideposts.detail: Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) rapidly closes the gap to the leaders. The peloton are right behind.

guideposts.label: Minimal gaps
guideposts.detail: With a flurry of attacks to shake the bunch, the leaders are only 5 seconds away. They have 7 kilometres to go to the summit.

guideposts.label: 9 leaders: Dunbar, Johannessen, Vermaerke, Zana...
guideposts.detail: Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step), Darren van Bekkum (XDS Astana) and José Luis Faura (Burgos Burpellet BH) join Ivo Oliveira, Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5), Bastien Tronchon (Groupama-FDJ United), Tobias Johannessen, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) into the final 4 kilometres of the climb. More counter-attackers set off from the bunch.

guideposts.label: Onley and Carapaz on the move?
guideposts.detail: Into the final kilometre of ascent, Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) follows a move. Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) also reacts.

guideposts.label: The average speed after 2 hours: 46.1 km/h
guideposts.detail: And that includes the ascent up Puerto de las Abejas!

guideposts.label: Results at Puerto de las Abejas (cat. 2, km 91)
guideposts.detail: 1. Leknessund, 5 pts 2. Vermaerke, 3 pts 3. Faura, 1 pt

guideposts.label: More attacks on the second climb of the day
guideposts.detail: Pau Miquel (Bahrain Victorious), Valentin Madouas, Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United), Sergio Samitier (Cofidis), Rudy Porter (Jayco AlUla), Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché) and Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL) are closing the gap to the 13 leaders up the Puerto del Viento (13.1km at 3.7%). The peloton are not far behind - Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike) attacks.

guideposts.label: Sepp Kuss also joins the front group
guideposts.detail: As Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike), Thomas Gloag (Pinarello Q36.5), Jan Hirt (NSN) and Harold Tejada (XDS Astana) join the front of the race, Netcompany Ineos pull the bunch a dozen of seconds behind.

guideposts.label: Dunbar leads the way, the attackers are caught
guideposts.detail: The Irishman is 10.5 km from the summit of the Puerto del Viento.

guideposts.label: The GC battle begins more than 100 kilometres from the finish
guideposts.detail: As a small group gets away, Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) gets on the move. Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) reacts, followed by Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), and then Enric Mas (Movistar).

guideposts.label: Dunbar still leads the way, a new group emerges
guideposts.detail: Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) will soon reach the summit and enter the final 100 kilometres of the stage. A group of chasers have set off with Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Thomas Gloag (Pinarello Q36.5), Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility)... More climbers attack from the bunch, including Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious).

guideposts.label: Dunbar leads the way to the summit
guideposts.detail: Not far behind, Buitrago is second with his polka dot jersey.

guideposts.label: Carapaz has attacked again!
guideposts.detail: The Ecuadorian icon is leading a small chase group over the top of the Puerto del Viento.

guideposts.label: The situation after 120 kilometres
guideposts.detail: The 17-man breakaway are on rolling terrain. +40'' Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), Jan Hirt (NSN), Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step), Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla), Larry Warbasse (Tudor), Gijs Leemreize (Picnic PostNL) Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) drives another chase group also featuring Marco Brenner (Tudor), Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM), Jorgen Nordhagen (Visma-Lease a Bike)... +1'2

guideposts.label: Rafferty suffers a mechanical while pulling for Carapaz
guideposts.detail: Richard Carapaz and his chase companions are 1'05'' behind the leaders and 20'' ahead of the bunch with 86 kilometres to go.

guideposts.label: Carapaz sits back and waits for the bunch
guideposts.detail: Among the chasers, Gijs Leemreize (Picnic PostNL) continues his effort to try and join the leaders.

guideposts.label: The situation after 130 kilometres of battle
guideposts.detail: There are 16 riders at the front (among the 17 riders previously announced, Rafferty dropped back). +1'05'' Leemreize +1'25'' Romeo paces the bunch

guideposts.label: The situation settles after a brutal first 3 hours
guideposts.detail: Gijs Leemreize (Picnic PostNL) has been cuaght by the bunch, now trailing by 2 minutes.
